title.en: Saying 'not' and 'cannot': 안, 못, and -지 마세요

summary.en: Simple negation with 안, inability with 못, and polite 'please don't' with -지 마세요.

body.en:
Korean distinguishes choosing not to do something (*안*) from being unable to do it because of circumstances (*못*).

Place *안* right before the verb or adjective for plain 'not': *안 가요* ('I'm not going'), *안 추워요* ('it isn't cold'). With '명사 + 하다' action verbs, *안* steps between the noun and *해요*: *일 안 해요* ('not working'), or uses the longer '-지 않아요' pattern (*보이지 않아요*, *흔들리지 않아요*).

Place *못* right before an action verb when something blocks you—lack of time, a stuck lock, or noise: *못 잤어요* ('couldn't sleep'), *못 바꿔요* ('cannot convert it').

For polite negative requests ('please don't ...'), attach '-지 마세요' to the verb stem: *걱정하지 마세요* ('please don't worry'), *열지 마세요* ('please don't open it').
